sentences.text: Really fun.
Was it nice and hot?
Pardon me?
Was it nice and hot?
Nice and sunny?
Yes, it was beautiful.
It was a little cool, but it's good for riding.
We were doing some horse showing and the weather was very beautiful and perfect.
So that was fun.
Good.
Who did you go with?
Your family?
Yes, My daughter was with us and my husband.
And her husband.
So it was really cool.
Can you hear me?
I can.
I can hear you absolutely fine.
Yeah.
Okay, I'm gonna try to turn up my volume.
Hold on just a sec.
All right, well.
Let me see if Jack is.
Can you hear me?
Okay, I got you now.
Fabulous.
Let me just see if Jackie is going to hop on the call.
He did say he was available.
Okay, great.
And how are you doing?
Yeah, I'm good.
I can't remember the last time we spoke.
I think I was already back in the uk, But I'm just speaking to all my American contact contacts in the last couple of weeks and just explaining that I am back in the UK at the moment.
Oh, you are?
I am, yeah.
Where is your permanent base?
In the uk, but we've got a five year visa for the US as well.
So we were in Los Angeles, Manhattan Beach.
I don't if you know it very well.
I love that area.
I just love California.
Yeah, me too.
Me too.
Hi, Jack.
Who's Jack?
Happy.
How's it going?
Hi.
Nice to see you again.
You too.
It's been a little while.
Must be about six months, I would say.
Is it?
Yep.
Well, things are really looking up.
I tried to keep Jack in the loop, but one of the things that is, that is happening, that is good for us is that our New York reps are starting to produce some pretty nice accounts.
We're working with Horizon Media, which is a huge agency in New York City, and they did some testing with us last year and now we are getting.
We just placed a million dollars with them for this quarter and I.
I believe that's going to increase, possibly double or triple for the next couple quarters.
They're very pleased with our activities.
They're switching their accounts from Ampersand, which is a huge billion dollar business that is our biggest competition.
We're seeing that begin to happen in a big way.
We have a couple national accounts that we think this rep and her staff are going to produce within the next, I would say 30 days.
We're projecting another million dollars from that activity.
And then we're starting with a couple fairly large New York agencies to develop our cost per acquisition streaming platform.
We have, I think, Two or three now that are pending.
The test will be small, but what we found is we start off with say 50,000 as we did with the Sunglass company, and it is now about a half a million every quarter.
So we're hoping that we can grow that business.
You know, the streaming is really where we're putting our focus.
Okay, so is that replacing the connected TV stuff or what?
Where are you going with sort of the trend in terms of where your business is?
The CTV is part of this cost per acquisition.
It is a CTV product that we're doing, but the clients pay per sale.
I don't know if you were familiar with per inquiry back in the day when people would advertise on television and pay per order.
It's very similar to that, but with our AI platform, it's very successful in finding where the activity is in real time.
And it's fraud free, which is.
Adds about 30% more activity to our impact to what we're doing.
So it's been pretty, pretty exciting.
Yeah, that sounds really good.
So you've had a lot of strong growth.
So I think things had been really strong for a long time.
And then you kind of just as we started talking about going to market, things started to dip.
So do you think you've replaced all of that business that you were losing?
Yeah, oh absolutely.
Already we, we have on the books equal to what we did all of last year.
Last year was hideous because of the political climate.
It was just like, oh my God, are we dying?
But we knew, we saw the light and we knew things were happening.
We were planting a lot of really good seeds.
Happened really fast.
We also have a very large agency in Los Angeles.
We met with them in Ocala, Florida.
They're course people go, go figure.
And they are developing major accounts.
They place 1.5 million in streaming with us.
Went across three days in December.
So that is a really.
All of this is looking so bright.
Yeah.
And like I said, we've already put on the books equal to what we did of all of last year and it's only the end of March.
So yeah, it's going great.
It's really going well.
And thank goodness because we were, we were really floundering last year, as you know.
Well, congratulations on turning things around so quickly.
So in terms of numbers then it wasn't quick.
We started developing a lot of this last year.
Like this time last year.
I've seen companies sort of disappear for three or four years before they can turn it around.
So I think you've done really well, thank you.
So what are we talking in terms of numbers for the full year?
If you were to 4x what you've done in Q1, what would that look like for the whole year?
I'm thinking between 25 and 30 million, which is, you know, the goal, considering the climate.
And we are lean and mean.
So the EBITDA will be, I think, pretty healthy.
I'm thinking between 2.5 to 3.
Okay, that's amazing.
So about.
You're looking at about 10%, 10% on it.
And is it.
Is that all agency spend or is that actual revenue that goes through the business at the 25 million?
It will.
The 25 million will be total spend, net revenue.
Net revenue.
Okay, well, okay, fantastic.
All right.
So that's a pretty strong margin.
And then in terms of where you are, Kathy, what.
What are you thinking?
Are you thinking that we should go back to market maybe in the summer, or do you think we should.
Yes, absolutely.
Okay.
Yeah, I'm thinking give us another three months to keep watering these plants that we've seeded.
And, you know, if we can get to the 30 million and the 3 EBITDA, I think that would be healthy enough to compensate for last year's loss.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
If you factor three, I want to be somewhere around at least 2.5 EBITDA if you're factoring three years.
Okay.
So I think a good time for us to revisit then would just be during those first couple of months of Q3.
And then if we went to market in September, because August is super quiet, as you know, everybody goes on holiday.
It's really difficult in the US to track everybody down.
But people come back to work in September and they're looking to get deals done before Christmas.
So I think that would be a good time for us to go to market.
But if we start the preparation in July, around that.
That point, and then we'll have everything ready from the six months, first six months of the year as well.
And hopefully that gives us you tracking the 3 million at that point.
So if you're 1.5 million EBITDA by the time we get to the end of June, that'd be.
Right.
So how do you factor and evaluate a company like ours?
What are you thinking?
Say we're at 2.5.
What factor would you use to evaluate the company?
Is it times seven, which is kind of what the marketplace historically has been, or do we reduce it because we're volatile?
So there are certain factors that will go in your favor and certain things that will go against you.
And so we kind of have to add minus on both sides to get to a multiple.

Volatility isn't fantastic, but if you can show sort of five or ten years of stable revenue but just one blip within that, then obviously the fact that you've turned it around so quickly kind of shows the strength of the business.
So it might not have a huge impact.
But also different types of businesses go up and down as well.
So I'm sure you'll appreciate the streaming market has been volatile as well around election years.
It can go up or down.
So that will all play into what the final multiple will look like, as will the size of the business and the size of your EBITDA as well.

But I would expect somewhere, look, without us sort of going into detail, because we would have to look into everything again, but I would expect somewhere between sort of 5 and 8 would be a reasonable sort of range for where you are.
You know, you're not a small business.
The margin is a little bit slim at 10%.
We would, we would see that as an opportunity maybe for a buyer that wanted to get rid of some duplication with another business that was similar.
So it wouldn't play against you necessarily, but it might put you somewhere in the middle of that range.
So at this stage, without over egging it, but also just being sort of conservative, there's somewhere between five and eight would sort of put us somewhere around six and a half, I would say, but.
But that's not to say that we couldn't get seven.
It's just about the confidence on the day that we go to market, really, whether we just wanted to push it as a 7x and see what the market responded with.
You know, at the end of the day, we can't.
We can only sell it for what somebody's prepared to pay for.
Right, right.
What would you say, Jack?
Jack's a bit more of an expert than I am.
Sounds about right.
There's a few factors that we can look at.
The volatility, as you say, Andy, is one of the pieces that we'd factor in.
We look at some recent comparables in the space.
There's been some big transactions in the space.
If we're justifying a high valuation, we can use those to prospective buyers.
Ultimately, it's about getting two offers on the table at the same time and driving a competitive process, really.
And the valuation range is really an indicator for a listing price to give buyers an idea of whether or not it's something that they can even put an Offering in for would be my sense.
So I think I'm pretty much just echoing what Andy says on that.
Okay, great.
And we'll take into account, you know, if you want to go to market at 7 as well.
I mean, I wouldn't say that's going to play too much against you, particularly if you can get to 3 million.
I would say it's pretty good multiple, so.
Yeah.
Okay.
Well, we got our work cut out for us.
We're okay until July, and then we're going to be super busy lounger somewhere.
Thank you for being so patient.
No worries.
No worries.
So why don't we.
We'll just put a note in our diary to get back to you on the 1st of July.
That gives you an opportunity to.
To get your books in order.
And we can set up a meeting mid July, I guess, once you've got things rounded off for Q2.
And then that gives us the summer months that are left to get everything ready and get you prepared, get your listing, get your marketing materials, etc.
And then we'll hit the ground running in September and get it sold.
That would be fantastic.
Okay, brilliant.
All right, well, we're all in agreement, it seems.
Yes.
Love it.
Love it.
So unless there's any.
Any other questions.
All right, thank you guys.
Okay.
Thank you, Jesse.
Thank you so much.
All right, Congratulations.
Speak soon.
Thank you.
Thank you.
It's been fun.
It's been fun.
I'll tell you.
A lot of work, but a lot of fun.
It's great when it works, right?
Yeah, definitely.
All right, you guys, thanks again for sticking by us and we'll make it happen.
Right?
Perfect.
All right, thanks.
Bye.
Jack, do you want to wait on for a sec?
Yeah.
Okay, so.

Prepare marketing materials and listing during summer months (13:25)
summary.overview: In the recent Business Strategy and Valuation discussion meeting for CTV Media, key insights revealed strong business recovery and growth, driven by significant account acquisitions in New York and collaborations with Horizon Media, which secured $1M for the current quarter. The company projects a potential 2-3x revenue increase in upcoming quarters, driven by a shift towards streaming platforms. Financial projections indicate expected revenue between $25-30M and an EBITDA margin of approximately 10%, aiming for improvements following a previously challenging year. The valuation discussion highlighted a target multiple of 6.5-7x EBITDA, reflecting market conditions and emphasizing a competitive process to attract multiple offers, with plans to enter the market by September after Q2 results. Action steps included preparing marketing materials during the summer and scheduling follow-up meetings in July to ensure alignment towards achieving a revenue goal of $30M and an EBITDA of $3M by the end of Q2.
summary.short_summary: The recent discussion on CTV Media's business strategy and valuation underscored a strong recovery and growth trajectory, fueled by significant account acquisitions in New York and strategic collaborations with Horizon Media, which secured $1M for the current quarter. The company anticipates a potential revenue increase of 2-3x in upcoming quarters, driven by a shift toward streaming platforms. Financial projections indicate expected revenues between $25-30M and an EBITDA margin of approximately 10%, aiming for improvements after a challenging previous year. The valuation discussion set a target multiple of 6.5-7x EBITDA, reflecting current market conditions, while emphasizing a competitive process to attract multiple offers, with plans to enter the market by September following Q2 results. Action steps include preparing marketing materials over the summer and scheduling follow-up meetings in July to align with a revenue goal of $30M and an EBITDA of $3M by the end of Q2.
